model_params.features: wave-12 feature set: the 10 time-domain statistics of the earlier waves (untouched) + 9 order-domain features (platform_lib.features.order): envelope-spectrum energy shares in +-2% bands at the bearing's BPFO, BPFI, BSF (ball-defect order = 2*ball-spin) and FTF characteristic orders and their 2nd harmonics, plus order-domain spectral entropy. Orders are computed per dataset from the actual bearing geometry (CWRU: SKF 6205-2RS JEM, 9 balls, Bd 0.3126 in, Pd 1.537 in -> BPFO 3.5848 / BPFI 5.4152 / BSF 4.7134 / FTF 0.3983; Paderborn: 6203, 8 balls, Bd 6.75 mm, Pd 28.55 mm -> BPFO 3.0543 / BPFI 4.9457 / BSF 3.9932 / FTF 0.3818) and each window is read at ITS recording's shaft speed, so the features are shaft-speed-relative by construction. Residual confounds, stated not hidden: true order resolution is 1/(revolutions per window) — 0.196 orders on CWRU windows (5.11 rev) but 1.25/2.08 orders on Paderborn windows (0.80 rev at N15, 0.48 rev at N09), coarser than the spacing between characteristic orders; slip moves true defect rates ~1-2% off the kinematic orders (hence the +-2% bands); rig transfer functions and sensor placement still differ.
model_params.training: fit on ALL cwru windows of the shared label set; no target data in training

split.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all cwru windows, tested on all paderborn windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']. Identical to the wave-5/9 transfer protocols — the ONLY change is the feature set (19 combined time + order).

preprocessing.feature_note: wave-12 feature set: the 10 time-domain statistics of the earlier waves (untouched) + 9 order-domain features (platform_lib.features.order): envelope-spectrum energy shares in +-2% bands at the bearing's BPFO, BPFI, BSF (ball-defect order = 2*ball-spin) and FTF characteristic orders and their 2nd harmonics, plus order-domain spectral entropy. Orders are computed per dataset from the actual bearing geometry (CWRU: SKF 6205-2RS JEM, 9 balls, Bd 0.3126 in, Pd 1.537 in -> BPFO 3.5848 / BPFI 5.4152 / BSF 4.7134 / FTF 0.3983; Paderborn: 6203, 8 balls, Bd 6.75 mm, Pd 28.55 mm -> BPFO 3.0543 / BPFI 4.9457 / BSF 3.9932 / FTF 0.3818) and each window is read at ITS recording's shaft speed, so the features are shaft-speed-relative by construction. Residual confounds, stated not hidden: true order resolution is 1/(revolutions per window) — 0.196 orders on CWRU windows (5.11 rev) but 1.25/2.08 orders on Paderborn windows (0.80 rev at N15, 0.48 rev at N09), coarser than the spacing between characteristic orders; slip moves true defect rates ~1-2% off the kinematic orders (hence the +-2% bands); rig transfer functions and sensor placement still differ.
preprocessing.windowing: non-overlapping 2048-sample windows in both datasets — the window TIME SPAN still differs by sampling rate: 2048 samples = 170.7 ms at CWRU's 12 kHz vs 32.0 ms at Paderborn's 64 kHz, i.e. 5.11 shaft revolutions vs 0.80 (N15) / 0.48 (N09). True order resolution is therefore 0.196 orders on CWRU but 1.25/2.08 orders on Paderborn — coarser than the spacing between the characteristic orders themselves; the order features on Paderborn windows are blunt by construction of the shared 2048-sample protocol.
preprocessing.excluded: CWRU 'Ball' class excluded (Paderborn scope has no ball-fault bearing); CWRU windows of that class are dropped from BOTH training (when CWRU is the source) and scoring
preprocessing.scaling: none (tree model, as in the wave-5/9 records)

notes: Zero-shot cwru -> paderborn bearing-fault transfer with the wave-12 order-domain feature set — the wave-5/9 transfer re-run with the feature set as the only changed variable. The order features align the characteristic defect frequencies of the two DIFFERENT bearings (6205 vs 6203) in shaft-speed-relative units, which neither the time-domain nor the rate-free spectral sets attempted. What remains unaligned, documented rather than corrected: rig transfer functions, sensor placement and mounting; load regimes; fault sizes/geometries; and — binding on the Paderborn side — a 2048-sample window holds less than one shaft revolution, so the true order resolution there (1.25-2.08 orders) is coarser than the order spacing. Both earlier baselines are carried in extra; the result is reported as measured, whether or not it improves.

reference_target_in_domain.protocol: MEASUREMENT-GROUPED split: GroupShuffleSplit by source_file (measurement id), 80/20, seed 42 — no measurement file contributes windows to both sides. NOTE: there is only ONE physical bearing per class

cwru.geometry_source: CWRU Bearing Data Center bearing information (drive-end test bearing SKF 6205-2RS JEM): 9 balls, ball diameter 0.3126 in, pitch diameter 1.537 in, contact angle 0 deg
cwru.bsf_convention: the `bsf` feature sits at 2*BSF (ball-defect repetition rate: a ball defect strikes both raceways once per ball revolution); `bsf_spin` is the pure ball spin frequency
cwru.speeds: per-recording: in-file X<id>RPM scalar where the file ships one (10 of 12 recordings, all 1796-1797 rpm); CWRU catalogue nominal by load otherwise (98.mat 1 hp -> 1772, 99.mat 2 hp -> 1750)

paderborn.geometry_source: 6203 nominal geometry as used for the Paderborn KAt-DataCenter bearing: 8 balls, ball diameter 6.75 mm, pitch diameter 28.55 mm, contact angle 0 deg
paderborn.bsf_convention: the `bsf` feature sits at 2*BSF (ball-defect repetition rate: a ball defect strikes both raceways once per ball revolution); `bsf_spin` is the pure ball spin frequency
paderborn.speeds: per-measurement nominal from the condition code (N15 -> 1500 rpm, N09 -> 900 rpm), cross-checked against the recorded speed channel (means 1499.6 / 899.7 rpm, std 0.18 rpm)

order_physics.band_definition: envelope-spectrum energy share within +-2% of the target order (8x zero-padded envelope spectrum; nearest single bin if the band holds no bin centre); normalised by total non-DC envelope-spectrum energy
